findings.title: â€” Actual native storage selection is never recognized (blocker).
findings.details:
`harness/Observation.ps1:102`, `Native-Witnesses`, expects `^Selected storage directory:`. The actual reopened native line is `[StorageDirs] :: Selected storage directory: ...`. Both retained RPTs use that form: multi-PBO line 1452 and instance-id-1 line 1442. Direct parsing of the full multi-PBO RPT recognizes four expected modules but zero selected-storage witnesses; a complete synthetic startup using the actual native prefix cannot trigger. Therefore even legitimate reviewed shutdown/error inputs cannot make the documented current controller satisfy native readiness on this retained format.

The test helper `Startup` instead manufactures an unprefixed storage line, and `Test-RuntimeAdapters` supplies that text through its replacement `Read-CurrentRpt`. Repair the exact source-backed storage envelope and add raw retained-line positive/wrong-path/duplicate tests through `Advance-Run` and the production read adapter. This is independent of the permitted unresolved native-shutdown prerequisite.

findings.title: â€” Pre-trigger SAVE violations are allowed, while incomplete private readiness can fail prematurely (high).
findings.details:
`Observation.ps1:183â€“202` permits `SAVE` among startup events, but validates only event shape and `Load-State` before returning `trigger`. The probes return `trigger` with `wroteLabel=false` on the existing pre-ready saves, and independently with `label=unknown-record`. `Save-State` checks those records only after exit. A run already showing a serialization failure or unknown entity can therefore receive a state-changing trigger before being rejected.

The same block calls `One-Event PRIVATE_INIT_READY/COMPILE_SMOKE` immediately once native evidence and the callback count are complete. Removing those not-yet-arrived script markers at T+45 produces `Expected exactly one PRIVATE_INIT_READY`, rather than pending startup evidence through its bound. Reopened historical logs do not establish that this particular polling split occurs natively; the deterministic controller behavior is nevertheless contrary to its documented complete-readiness gate. Validate every already-observed record and failure before trigger, while treating only legitimately incomplete positive readiness as pending. Add both delayed-arrival completion and deadline failure routes.

findings.title: â€” Deferred seed IDs bypass nonzero SAVE identity uniqueness (high).
findings.details: `Protocol.ps1:247â€“277,307â€“346,400â€“416` constructs the seed oracle from setter records. When setters report all-zero IDs, every canonical field remains null. `Save-State:320â€“321` consequently skips PID equality, and never applies `Pids` uniqueness to the post-ready save set. Three distinct labels can all save `persistentId=99/0/0/0` and `Phase-State` accepts the seed. The probe uses full valid event fields and phase observations; it does not rely on malformed old fixtures. Retain the permitted same-v1 adoption policy, but reject duplicate nonzero identities and conflicting known observations throughout the seed SAVE evidence before publishing its success. Do not invent native PID assignment timing.

findings.title: â€” An incomplete fabricated success still authorizes the DAG (high).
findings.details:
`Storage.ps1:206â€“244`, `Read-Success`, validates several outcome fields and ancestor hashes, but treats empty `immutableInputs` and `logs` as valid and `logRoot` as optional. It never requires the full production receipt schema, native/process timing, process disposal/port release, review/config/context/source identities or oracle evidence appropriate to that phase. A small fabricated no-mod receipt with outcome flags, matching wrapper/attempt hashes, and empty input/log arrays passes `Gate smoke-v1` despite containing none of those witnesses.

This probe does not claim hashes can authenticate arbitrary hostile authors. It demonstrates acceptance of a structurally incomplete receipt that the gate is specifically meant to reject; the authorâ€™s `New-SyntheticSuite` deliberately constructs similarly reduced receipts. Enforce a typed complete success schema and exact required input/log sets, bind and revalidate the produced observations under the suiteâ€™s reviewed policy, and keep reduced synthetic adapters distinct from production receipt validation. Preserve the existing checks for failed bodies, changed ancestors and repeated attempts.

findings.title: â€” Altered active-mission metadata permits writes outside the owned root (high).
findings.details:
`Runtime.ps1:83â€“103` reopens source/package/mission/executable manifests, but does not enforce the derived `activeMission` location. `Set-ActiveMission:147â€“169` uses that field directly; its existing-target branch performs no containment check before overwriting mutable files. The stronger probe copies a real prepared synthetic suite manifest, changes only its suite identity and `activeMission`, passes the real `Open-Suite`, acquires an ordinary lease for the simulated work root, and replaces an existing init file outside that work root with the v1 mission.

Every path touched by this probe is inside the review evidence directory; no actual shared mission was modified. A suite hash supplied for review is not a substitute for enforcing the controllerâ€™s non-negotiable confinement rules. Require the exact derived active location, ordinary physical ancestors, source/destination separation and ownership of every destination before every mutation, including the existing-target branch. Recheck other stored path/config/port fields against their derived contract when opening the suite.

findings.title: â€” Current RPT consumption bypasses physical-file validation (high).
findings.details: `Runtime.ps1:245â€“257`, `Read-CurrentRpt`, enumerates one RPT and calls `ReadAllText` without `File`/`Path-Chain`. A hardlinked RPT referring to a separate reviewer-owned sentinel is accepted at consumption. Post-exit hashing may eventually reject the link, but the unvalidated content has already entered the native/trigger gate. This is distinct from the correctly rejecting standalone `File` hardlink and junction tests. Apply the production physical-path checks to the current profile and RPT at every read, before deriving authority from their bytes; test both hardlink and reparse inputs at this consumer.

findings.title: â€” Final journal failure leaves a passed authorization behind (high).
findings.details:
`Dispatch.ps1:134â€“145` updates a failed attempt before it attempts the final dispatch-journal write. If that last write throws, the catch sets only `summary.passed=false`; the attempt and success ledger remain passed, and `Read-Success` does not consult a completed dispatch receipt. The independent fake-run adapter executes the actual dispatch bookkeeping with only process outcome/preflight and the final journal write substituted: the dispatch throws, yet a subsequent real `Gate smoke-v1` accepts its no-mod prerequisite.

This is an ordinary exception-path defect, not merely a forged-file scenario. Publish authorization only after all required completion bookkeeping is durable, or make later failures invalidate it in a way every consuming gate checks. Preserve the failure even if its preferred journal destination fails; do not leave the rootâ€™s inactive owner and passed ledger as sufficient continuation evidence. Add final-journal, attempt-update, owner-update, freeze, closure and release-failure regressions against the actual dispatch sequence.
